title: TiRex-2: Generalizing TiRex to Multivariate Data and Streaming
claim: Existing models each lack key capabilities; ours is the only one that provides every desired property at once.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right, stacked feature rows with green checks versus red crosses

abstract: We introduce TiRex-2, a recurrent xLSTM-based time series foundation model that generalizes the univariate TiRex to multivariate forecasting with both past and future covariates. Real-world forecasting is inherently sequential: observations arrive continuously, variables evolve jointly, and a subset of covariates is known ahead of time. Existing Transformer-based time series foundation models capture cross-variate dependencies, but the cost of ingesting each new observation grows at least linearly with context length, even with KV caching. TiRex-2 addresses these limitations with a memory-centric recurrent design built around an asymmetric group-attention variate mixer: paired with a bidirectional time mixer, it integrates future-known covariates while keeping target variables strictly causal. To our knowledge no other time series foundation model does both, and it is what makes streaming at constant per-patch cost possible. For scalable multivariate pretraining, we propose a synthetic coupling pipeline that composes multivariate samples on the fly from large univariate corpora. On GIFT-Eval, TiRex-2 improves on the zero-shot Chronos-2-Synth on all four statistics, and on Chronos-2 under a matched corpus. On fev-bench Chronos-2 stays ahead on skill score at $2.2\times$ the mean active parameters. TiRex-2 uses 38.4M active parameters in univariate mode, plus 44.1M for multivariate forecasting. Code is available at https://github.com/NX-AI/tirex-2 .
